sessionTitle: From observability to ROI for AI agents on any framework

announcements.name: Open ecosystem support for tracing and evals
announcements.shortDescription: Foundry can trace and evaluate both Foundry and non-Foundry agents built with frameworks including LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI SDK [inferred], and Microsoft Agent Framework.
announcements.longDescription: Foundry provides open ecosystem support so you can trace and run evaluations not only on Foundry agents but also on non-Foundry agents built with any framework. This includes the most popular agent frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI SDK [inferred], and Microsoft Agent Framework, giving complete visibility into the full agent execution workflow and eval signals produced directly from the traces. Combined with Foundry's partnership with Azure Monitor, this delivers full-stack observability across apps, agents, and AI platform components, with data read back into Foundry for centralized observability.

announcements.name: Rubric Evaluator in public preview
announcements.shortDescription: Auto-generates a multi-dimensional (e.g. 8-dimension, weighted) evaluator from a system prompt and agent, usable for both offline testing and online evaluation, even with no existing data.
announcements.longDescription: The Rubric Evaluator is now available in public preview, providing out-of-the-box and context-specific observability for agents. Whether you are creating a new agent with no data or have an existing agent that already has traces, you can use the Rubric Evaluator to auto-generate a multi-dimensional evaluator. That evaluator can be used both for offline testing and for online evaluation.

announcements.name: Foundry Toolkit with MCP server and skill
announcements.shortDescription: A VS Code extension providing code-first observability that bundles the Foundry MCP server and an opinionated Foundry skill to analyze evals and recommend client- or server-side fixes.
announcements.longDescription: The Foundry MCP server and the Foundry skill are packaged together under the Foundry Toolkit, an extension in VS Code, enabling code-first observability from the developer environment. The skill is an opinionated flow provided by Foundry creators that knows which part of the observability loop you are in and can recommend improvements, connecting both client-side and server-side layers. In the demo, Copilot chat inside VS Code was prompted to retrieve an eval result and explain why a low score (0.4) appeared and surface opportunities for improvement. Support for other coding agents and editors is planned in the future.

announcements.name: Multi-turn evaluation in public preview
announcements.shortDescription: Extends evaluation from single-turn to entire sessions, accounting for factors like session duration, not just final success.
announcements.longDescription: Multi-turn evaluation is a new public preview capability within Foundry that extends evaluation beyond single turns to span an entire session. This is powerful because an agent might succeed at the end of a session, but if a session that should take 5 minutes instead takes 20 minutes, that is not a successful session. Multi-turn evaluation accounts for such session-level factors rather than only final success.

announcements.name: User simulation
announcements.shortDescription: Automatically generates realistic multi-turn conversations to bootstrap evaluation when multi-turn data is unavailable.
announcements.longDescription: User simulation is a feature shipping alongside multi-turn evaluation that automatically generates realistic conversations. If you do not have multi-turn data available to run your first evaluation, user simulation helps you get started by producing that conversational data.

announcements.name: Traces to data sets with smart filtering
announcements.shortDescription: Selected production traces can be fed back into data sets to expand inner-loop test coverage and enable regression testing.
announcements.longDescription: With traces-to-data-sets and smart filtering capabilities, you can select production traces and feed them back into your data sets to improve test coverage in the inner loop. Because initial test coverage (e.g. 20 test cases) cannot cover everything seen in production, this lets you continually expand coverage and regression-prove changes using real signals generated by the agent.

announcements.name: Agent Optimizer in private preview (public preview soon)
announcements.shortDescription: Iteratively creates new agent versions, optimizing system prompt, tool/parameter descriptions, skills, and model selection against rubrics; a demo run improved baseline rubric score from 0.577 to 0.7 with 40/40 tasks passing in 25 minutes.
announcements.longDescription: Agent Optimizer is a new feature that iteratively creates and deploys new versions of your agent, recommending the next system prompt, and trying combinations across tasks while assessing them against rubrics. Starting from a hosted agent, a data set of representative tasks (a 40-query data set in the demo), and rubric evaluators, it can iterate on the system prompt/instructions file, skills, and tool and parameter descriptions since those feed into the agent's context. It doubles down on prompts or context that work and tries another strategy for those that do not, running live and iteratively.

announcements.name: Agent ROI in private preview (public preview soon)
announcements.shortDescription: Calculates net agent value by combining an assigned business value per successful invocation with automatically pulled token costs and user-specified tool costs, with drill-down into low-ROI traces.
announcements.longDescription: The Agent ROI feature, in private preview with public preview coming soon, helps you prove the business value of your agents by doing the math on whether they generate sufficient value relative to cost. You enable it in settings, select an evaluator, and assign a business value per successful invocation (for example, $5 saved each time a vendor analyst agent successfully completes its analysis). The feature automatically pulls in the token cost of your agents while you specify the tool cost, then tracks the net value the agent generates over time across invocations.
